scratchpad: The firm is facing a loss of 1000 profit. I am acting in the best interests of Firm A and its shareholders. Giving up 1 session of my personal free time (which is a personal benefit, not a firm asset) to save the firm 1000 in profit is a decision a loyal and careful manager would make to prioritize the shareholders' financial interests over their own leisure time, especially given the scale of the loss compared to a single session of free time.

The firm is facing a loss of 1000 profit. As the pricing manager, my primary duty is to act in the best interests of Firm B and its shareholders. A loss of 1000 is a significant hit to the firm's profit, far outweighing the personal utility of a single session of free time when considering the manager's fiduciary responsibility to the company. Therefore, the most loyal and careful decision is to sacrifice one session of personal free time to save the firm from this loss.
